data.title: Theriva™ Biologics Announces Reverse Stock Split
data.description:
ROCKVILLE, Md., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Theriva™ Biologics, Inc. (NYSE American: TOVX), a diversified clinical-stage company developing therapeutics designed to treat cancer and related diseases in areas of high unmet need, announced today a reverse stock split of its authorized and issued and outstanding common stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a ratio of one (1) share of common stock for every thirty (30) shares of common stock, effective as of 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on December 1, 2026 (the “Effective Date”).

The Company’s common stock will begin trading on a split-adjusted basis when the market opens on December 2, 2026. The reverse stock split was authorized by the Company’s Board of Directors on November 13, 2026. Pursuant to the laws of the State of Nevada, the Company’s state of incorporation, the Company’s Board of Directors has the authority to effect a reverse stock split without shareholder approval if the number of authorized shares of common stock and the number of outstanding shares of common stock are proportionally reduced. The Company will file a certificate of change to its articles of incorporation, as amended, with the Secretary of State of Nevada to effect the reverse stock split. The Company’s common stock will continue to trade on the NYSE American under the stock ticker “TOVX” but will trade under the new CUSIP number 87164U607.

As a result of the reverse split, each thirty (30) pre-split shares of common stock outstanding will automatically combine into one (1) new share of common stock without any action on the part of the holders, and the number of outstanding common shares will be reduced from 45,892,668 shares to approximately 1,529,756 shares without taking into account fractional shares. The number of authorized shares of common stock will be proportionally reduced from 350,000,000 shares to 11,666,666 shares.

The reverse stock split is being effected to ensure that the Company can meet the per share price requirements of the NYSE American, the Company's current listing exchange.

No fractional shares will be issued as a result of the reverse stock split. Stockholders who otherwise would be entitled to a fractional share because they hold a number of shares not evenly divisible by the one (1) for thirty (30) reverse split ratio will automatically be entitled to receive an additional fractional share of the Company’s common stock to round up to the next whole share.

Proportionate adjustments will also be made to the number of shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of, and the exercise price of, the Company’s outstanding warrants and stock options, and to the number of shares of common stock reserved for issuance under the Company’s equity incentive plans.

The Company’s transfer agent, Equiniti Trust Company, which is also acting as the exchange agent for the reverse split, will send instructions to stockholders of record who hold stock certificates regarding the exchange of their old certificates for new certificates, should they wish to do so. Stockholders who hold their shares in brokerage accounts or “street name” are not required to take action to effect the exchange of their shares.

About Theriva™ Biologics, Inc.

Theriva™ Biologics (NYSE American: TOVX) is a diversified clinical-stage company developing therapeutics designed to treat cancer and related diseases in areas of high unmet need. The Company’s subsidiary Theriva Biologics, S.L., has been developing a new oncolytic adenovirus platform designed for intravenous (IV), intravitreal and intratumoral delivery to trigger tumor cell death, improve access of co-administered cancer therapies to the tumor, and promote a robust and sustained anti-tumor response by the patient’s immune system. The Company’s lead clinical-stage candidate is VCN-01 (zabilugene almadenorepvec), an oncolytic adenovirus designed to replicate selectively within tumor cells, and to degrade the tumor stroma barrier that serves as a significant physical and immunosuppressive barrier to cancer treatment. For more information, please visit Theriva™ Biologics’ website at www.therivabio.com.

data.title: Micron and Sandisk stocks might look like bargains, but analysts say that's actually a red flag
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

Cheap valuation multiples for memory stocks have historically been associated with peak pricing levels, according to analysts

Shares of Micron fell nearly 14% on Friday.

Memory stocks were among the biggest decliners as the technology sector bled red ink on Friday.

Shares of Micron Technology (MU) closed down 14% on Friday, while shares of Sandisk (SNDK) fell 16%. Western Digital's stock (WDC) sank 12%.

The pressure on these stocks is mounting. Micron shares are down 50.99% from their peak, while Sandisk shares are down 72.85% from their highs and Western Digital's stock has shed 64.97%.

The chip sector in general has been hit hard due to various factors. Those include concerns that politicians could get stricter about data-center construction, leadership uncertainty at Nvidia (NVDA) and the idea that Anthropic's (ANT) IPO might have sucked attention away from the broader tech sector.

Then there is the perennial debate over the price-to-earnings multiples of memory stocks.

Micron and Sandisk shares both trade at meaningful discounts to their recent historical valuations. Micron's stock trades at 3.76 times estimated earnings for the next 12 months, versus a two-year average of 9.10 times. Sandisk's multiple of 3.04 times forward earnings expectations is below its 10.47-times average since the time of its separation from Western Digital in February 2025.

But Brendan Burke, the research director for semiconductors, supply chain and emerging tech at the Futurum Group, says that low price-to-earnings ratios for memory stocks are a "warning label, not a bargain sign."

"Investors have learned over decades to sell memory stocks at peak earnings, because the earnings side of that ratio has historically collapsed when the cycle turns," he said.

"A multiple in the low single digits tells you the market is pricing today's profits as a peak," he added.

Admittedly, there are some caveats. The historical precedent "ignores that AI has changed the shape of this cycle." Some types of memory, like high-bandwidth memory and solid-state-drive storage, are tied to what he called "mission-critical data-center buildouts," as opposed to memory for PCs and handsets. That distinction means the earnings might be "more durable than these multiples imply," Burke said.

William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji told MarketWatch that there's a limit to the usefulness of low P/E ratios as a "valuation support metric."

Memory stocks often see "extreme volatility in pricing," CreditSights analyst Andy Li added, and that can lead to boom-and-bust cycles.

If investors assume the market is still cyclical, a "dramatic price decline may well be in the cards," he said. "The price action reflects that fear."

Li explained that cyclical stocks like memory often top with "very low" price-to-earnings multiples, because that's when their estimated earnings for the next 12 months are "most inflated." Meanwhile, they also bottom with relatively high multiples, following the same logic, he said.

Separately, he added that the fact that monthly options expire on Friday could also be a technical factor affecting the stocks.

-Hannah Pedone

data.title: Wall St ends sharply lower on AI selloff, S&P 500, Dow in correction
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes: Dow down 1.93%, S&P 500 off 3.70%, Nasdaq down 5.28%
  • Anthropic down 9.1% a day after debut
  • Intuit falls after it cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit
  • Caterpillar drops on demand concerns for AI-related energy generation equipment
  • Cryptocurrency firms slide on bitcoin weakness

By Stephen Culp and Utkarsh Hathi

US stocks extended their rout on Friday, and the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections after Anthropic's momentous debut fell flat, exacerbating worries about the AI trade that has driven this year's stock market rally.

All three major US equity indexes ended sharply lower. The Dow and the S&P 500 are now more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming both indexes have entered a correction.

The bellwether S&P 500 notched its seventh consecutive drop, its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The S&P 500 and the Dow logged their largest weekly percentage losses since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling "liberation day" tariff package.

The Nasdaq's weekly drop was its largest since March 2020. The tech-heavy index has dipped into negative territory for the year.

"This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, appears to be accelerating to a certain degree," said Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management in Billings, Montana. "But as we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day today."

"Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate space, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time," Northey added, referring to economic strength and solid corporate earnings, among other things.

Anthropic's supersized debut as a publicly held company, which was intended to raise as much as $2 trillion in market cap, failed to catch fire on Thursday, closing 17.1% above its $83 offer price as enthusiasm for the stock faded throughout the session.

In its second day as a publicly held company, Anthropic's shares fell 9.1%. Nvidia's shares tumbled 13.8%.

The Anthropic IPO, combined with Nvidia's quarterly earnings report, failed to dispel fears over risks associated with artificial intelligence and the massive expenditures on the nascent technology.

"Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right," said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services in Hammond, Indiana. "A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn't."

The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index <.SOX>, which has powered much of the broader stock market's gains in recent months, was up as much as 106.6% in mid-June. That luster has faded, with the index's year-to-date advance having shrunk to 18.7%.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon fell 3.9%, while Meta dropped 5.9%.

Neocloud firm CoreWeave fell 12.1% and its peer Nebius slid 16.1%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average <.DJI> fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33, the S&P 500 <.SPX> lost 265.41 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.42 and the Nasdaq Composite <.IXIC> lost 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

The CBOE Market Volatility Index <.VIX>, often referred to as Wall Street's "fear gauge," rose to its highest close since April 7, 2025.

INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank's policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels.

Markets are pricing a near-certain likelihood of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike at the Fed's next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.

Among other movers, Intuit shares fell 12.8% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.

UnitedHealth rose 2.8% after TD Cowen upgraded its shares to a "buy" from a "hold" rating.

The AI selloff also sent Caterpillar 5% lower on worries over weakening demand for its power-generating and backup power equipment.

Cryptocurrency firms including Coinbase , Strategy and Robinhood tumbled between 6.3% and 9.6% after bitcoin dropped below the $60,000 level.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.77-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 38 new highs and 1,199 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 928 stocks rose and 3,964 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4.27-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 28 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 21 new highs and 826 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 25.19 billion shares, compared with the 19.50 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Bloom Energy Supports Lincoln Fire & Rescue Ahead of Ohio State-Nebraska Matchup
data.description:
As Lincoln gets ready for the Ohio State-Nebraska matchup, Bloom Energy is joining the community off the field to recognize the firefighters and first responders who help keep Nebraska’s capital safe.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120207460/en/

On Friday, Bloom Energy visited Lincoln Fire & Rescue Station #1 and presented the department with a $10,000 donation. The contribution recognizes the more than 300 Lincoln Fire & Rescue personnel serving the city across 16 fire stations and supports the department’s continued work protecting the Lincoln community.

“Lincoln’s firefighters have been called on in extraordinary ways this year, from responding to historic flooding to helping fight the largest wildfire in Nebraska’s history,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “We’re proud to recognize Lincoln Fire & Rescue and support the men and women who protect this community every day.”

“We’re very grateful to Bloom Energy for this opportunity. Employee well being is critical at Lincoln Fire and Rescue, but it’s not always something we have a lot of funding for when we also have equipment and other operational needs to prioritize,” said Dave Engler, Fire Chief, Lincoln Fire & Rescue. “This funding will allow us to invest directly in our members, whether that’s through physical and behavioral health programs, training and support following critical incidents, or resources to address challenges that come with shift work. We’re excited to put these dollars toward the health and well-being of our firefighters.”

Lincoln Fire & Rescue provides emergency services and community programs across the city. Its members also serve on specialized response teams, including Nebraska Task Force One.

This year, Lincoln firefighters have responded well beyond their day-to-day duties. In March, a Fire & Rescue crew deployed to Ogallala to help fight the largest wildfire in Nebraska’s history. In October, crews including the department’s Water Rescue Team rescued more than a dozen people during the flooding.

The donation reflects Bloom Energy’s commitment to supporting the communities it serves and recognizing the people and organizations that run essential services.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Ohio State-Nebraska game as ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Lincoln.

data.description:
Key points:
  • Colombia's 2026 fiscal deficit to surpass 7.6% of GDP, finance minister says
  • BofA sees scope for renewed capital inflows into Brazil
  • Mexican retail sales signal softer domestic demand
  • Argentina's country risk climbs to a 13-month high, bonds collapse

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Avinash P

Latin American assets were on track for weekly losses on Friday as a global retreat from risk assets intensified after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI trade, while softer commodity prices also weighed.

While Latin American markets have limited direct exposure to the technology sector, the deterioration in global risk sentiment spilled over into the region.

"The tech-led decline spread across regions, prompting a flight to safe-haven that lifted US Treasuries and the Japanese yen, while copper hit its lowest level since March and gold extended its rout," Citi analysts said in a note.

Currencies in the region remained under stress as the dollar's strength persisted, with investors seeking the safety of greenback-denominated assets including Treasuries, weakening the appeal of riskier emerging market assets.

MSCI's index of Latin American equities (.MILA00000PUS) fell 1.2%, languishing at a more than one-year low, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) fell 0.8% and was on track for its fourth consecutive weekly loss.

In Mexico, the peso fell 0.5%, while stocks eased 0.1%.

Investors took note of a potentially positive development on the trade front as EU agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen said he expects Mexico to clear the final hurdle for a new EU trade pact, bringing Mexican and European interests closer together.

Meanwhile, Mexican retail sales fell in September from the previous month, data from the national statistics agency showed.

Argentina's sovereign risk premium rose above 1,000 basis points on Friday, its highest level since October 2025, as a sell-off in government bonds intensified and weighed on the peso.

The country's dollar bonds fell more than 2 cents on the dollar across the curve, while the peso dropped 0.9%.

Markets in the region's largest economy, Brazil, were closed for a holiday. The Brazilian real was down 0.24% against the US dollar on Friday on very low volume.

Investors continue to closely monitor domestic developments. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is nearing a decision on his next finance minister, with an announcement possible as early as next week, according to six sources familiar with the discussions.​‌

Separately, Bank of America said there remains a potential path for capital inflows to return to Latin America's largest economy despite a challenging economic environment at home and abroad.

In Colombia, the benchmark stocks index was flat, while the peso weakened to a five-month low, down 2.3%.

Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said Colombia's 2026 fiscal deficit will exceed 7.6% of gross domestic product, above the 7.2% set out in the country's recent budget.

Broader global factors also weighed on sentiment. Commodity prices fell, with gold down over 2% and copper headed for its biggest weekly drop in 19 months.

Chile's peso depreciated 0.6% to 1,022.08 per dollar, its weakest level in more than four years, as lower copper prices weighed on the currency of the world's largest copper producer.

Separately, Polish central banker Joanna Tyrowicz told PAP News Agency that interest rates should be "much higher" and that the central bank's communication should remain "hawkish".

data.title: U.S. Stocks Plummet To Seven-Month Lows As Anthropic Plunges
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Following the steep losses seen during Thursday's session, stocks showed an even more substantial move to the downside during trading on Friday. The major averages went into a tailspin as the day progressed, closing sharply lower.

The Nasdaq plummeted 1,261.47 points or 5.3 percent to a seven-month closing low of 22,617.73, turning negative for the year.

The S&P 500 also plunged 265,44 points or 3.7 percent to 6,910.39, while the Dow slumped 949.73 points or 1.9 percent to 48,147.33. Both indexes also hit their lowest closing levels in seven months.

For the week, the Nasdaq nosedived by 10 percent, the S&P 500 plummeted by 8.6 percent and the Dow plunged by 8 percent.

The sell-off on Wall Street came amid continued weakness among technology stocks, as reflected by the particularly steep drop by the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

A steep drop by shares of Anthropic (ANT) weighed on the tech sector following its record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday.

Shares of Anthropic plunged by more than 9 percent after the Claude developer spiked by 17.1 percent on Thursday but ended the day well off its highs of the session.

'The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

She added, 'The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run.'

Concerns about the outlook for interest rates may also have contributed to the selling pressure, with at least a quarter point rate hike seen as a near-certainty at the Federal Reserve's monetary policy next month.

Following hawkish comments from several Fed officials, traders have grown increasingly worried the central bank will continue to raise rates in the coming months in order to combat stubborn inflation.

Sector News

Semiconductor stocks turned in some of the market's worst performances on the day, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plummeting by 10.7 percent to a seven-month closing low.

Computer hardware and networking stocks also saw substantial weakness, dragging the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index and the NYSE Arca Networking Index down by 8 percent and 7.8 percent, respectively.

Outside of the tech sector, gold stocks extended the recent sell-off amid an extended nosedive by the price of the precious metal. Reflecting the weakness in the sector, the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index plunged by 5.2 percent.

Brokerage, oil service and airline stocks also saw considerable weakness, moving lower along with most of the other major sectors.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved sharply lower during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index dove by 5.1 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index tumbled by 1.2 percent.

The major European markets also showed significant moves to the downside. While the German DAX Index plunged by 2.6 percent, the French CAC 40 Index slumped by 1.9 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index slid by 1 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries skyrocketed amid the extended sell-off on Wall Street. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has plunged 12.0 basis points to 4.932 percent.

data.title: Anthropic Barely Dodges Broken IPO Status — Market Talk
data.description: A day after snagging the "biggest ever" initial public offering crown from SpaceX, Anthropic very nearly picks up the more dubious distinction of biggest ever broken IPO. An IPO is considered broken if a stock trades below its offering price shortly after the offering. Anthropic shares end the day down 8.5% at $88.91 after falling to as low as $83.05, nearly breaking its $83 IPO price. SpaceX shares, priced at $135 in June, reached a high of $225.64 shortly after the IPO before falling below $135 the following month and closing Friday at $127.79. The 10 biggest U.S. IPOs this year prior to Anthropic's were trading on average more than 20% below their offer prices, the Financial Times reported earlier this week. (colin.kellaher@wsj.com)
